input.summary:
P3 west bedroom (parts/room-27.mjs): removed the lantern-on-table layer at y8, the one write that landed in roof cell (53,8,19) deepslate_tiles; header comment updated to match.
./make.sh exits 0 and the part's line now shows only "10 placed", with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE. The off-palette list was already empty for this part.
mcd light on the room: 15 floor cells, min 9, no dark cells, so the south end still reads lit without the table lamp.
left: The lantern that stood on the table top at (53,7,19) is gone, so the south end has no lamp of its own. Light still reaches it (min 9), but a lamp is missing from the design; it could sit elsewhere if the designer wants one.
I overwrote run.log in the run directory with the make.sh output; it was there before this job and its old contents are not kept.

waste.what: Working out which cell the refused write hit: I had to match the REFUSED coordinate (53,8,19) to the layer row and column by hand (layers rows run +z, columns +x) and then guess what roof part had put there.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and a manual coordinate check
waste.tool: A make.sh/runParts report that gives the row and column of each refused cell in the layers() string, and names the earlier part that owns it (e.g. 'roofs'), would have pointed straight at the layer and row to remove.

waste.what: Deciding whether the removed lamp left the room dark. I ran the light check by hand after the rebuild.
waste.tool: runParts could print the room's min light (mcd light --only) next to each part's placed/refused line, so a fix that drops a light source shows at once.

waste.what: Confirming the off-palette check was clean by reading parts-report.json directly, because make.sh's tail showed only the REFUSED message.
waste.tool: make.sh's per-part line could state 'offPalette: none' as well as the refused count, so both checks read from one line.
